Set(string) -- Set the material.
The material must be one of the following values: Brass, Bronze, Copper, Gold, Pewter, Plaster, Plastic, Silver, Steel, Stone, Shiny plastic, Satin, Metalized, Neon GNC, Chrome, Aluminium, Obsidian, Neon PHC, Jade, Ruby or Emerald.

Whether the values carry the PBR reading rather than the Phong one: DiffuseColor is the base colour, Shininess the roughness, SpecularColor the F0 tint with the metallic factor in its alpha.
Setting it CONVERTS the values, so the surface keeps looking like itself in the other model; only the specular colour, which Phong alone can state, is lost on the way back. Materials read from a ShapeAppearance list carry the list's mode, and assigning materials to one gives it the mode of the first -- the list holds a single mode, so any further entry is converted to it.
The metallic factor, riding the specular alpha. Reads 0 on a Phong material, which has no metals; writing one converts the material to PBR first, since stating a metallic factor decides the mode.
The roughness. On a Phong material it reads as the Blinn-Phong derivation of the shininess; writing one converts the material to PBR first, as Metallic does.

The surface finish pattern by name: "" (none), "knurl", "knurl-straight", "brushed", "blasted" or "turned". An unrecognised name reads back as "".
A finish states what was done to the surface, not how it shades, so it survives every conversion between the Phong and PBR readings. Size it with FinishPitch, FinishDepth and FinishAngle; setting the pattern to "" clears all three.
Surface finish feature spacing, in millimetres.
Surface finish peak to valley depth, in millimetres.
Surface finish lay direction in degrees, within the pattern frame. A lay has an axis rather than a direction, so the value wraps into [0, 180).

The embedded texture image of the material, as the string upstream FreeCAD stores it in. Nothing in this fork writes one; it is here so a material that arrived carrying one survives a round trip through Python rather than being silently dropped by anything that restates the material -- the property editor's appearance row among them.
The path of the material's texture image. Carried, not used, exactly like Image.
The identity of the material card this material came from. Carried, not used, exactly like Image -- and it is what makes two appearances the same appearance whatever their colours currently say.
